judged_text: The newBookingId merge path still picks oldCalendarEvent with references.find while calendarReference in the same function was converted to a filter over all references. Rescheduling a multi-host collective booking into an existing booking deletes only the first host's old calendar event; the other hosts' old events are orphaned and keep the old slot busy.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `calendarReference` was changed from a single reference (via `.find`) to an array of all calendar references (via `.filter`) and the update loop now processes all of them. However, in the merge path `if (newBookingId) { ... }`, the code still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`, which selects only the first calendar reference for deletion. With multi-calendar/multi-host behavior introduced elsewhere in the diff (e.g., destinationCalendar becoming an array and multiple events being created), this would leave other old calendar events undeleted/orphaned when merging/rescheduling.
